snapshot.description: Bootstrap model establishing ecosystem and environment identities.

entities.name: MSYS2
entities.summary: Software distribution and development environment for Windows.

entities.name: msys-2.0.dll
entities.summary: MSYS2 POSIX compatibility runtime.

entities.name: GNU Bash
entities.summary: The GNU Bourne-Again shell, packaged in the MSYS environment as the default interactive and login command interpreter.

entities.name: GNU Coreutils
entities.summary: The GNU core utilities collection, packaged in the MSYS environment as the primary POSIX-oriented file, shell, and text manipulation command set.

properties.role: core file, shell, and text utilities

entities.name: GNU Grep
entities.summary: The GNU string-search utility, packaged in the MSYS environment for BRE/ERE/PCRE pattern matching over text streams and files.

properties.role: pattern search over text streams and files

entities.name: GNU Sed
entities.summary: The GNU stream editor, packaged in the MSYS environment for scripted, non-interactive text transformation.

entities.name: GNU Awk (gawk)
entities.summary: GNU's implementation of the POSIX awk pattern-scanning and processing language, packaged in the MSYS environment and providing the `awk` command.

entities.name: GNU Findutils
entities.summary: The GNU file-finding utilities, packaged in the MSYS environment for predicate-based filesystem traversal and command construction over found files.

properties.role: filesystem traversal and command construction over found files

entities.name: GNU Tar
entities.summary: The GNU archiving utility, packaged in the MSYS environment for storing, backing up, and transporting file trees as a single archive stream.

entities.name: GNU Gzip
entities.summary: The GNU compression utility, packaged in the MSYS environment for single-file DEFLATE-based compression, commonly paired with tar.

entities.name: bzip2
entities.summary: A Burrows-Wheeler-based single-file compression utility, packaged in the MSYS environment and split from its shared library, libbz2.

entities.name: XZ Utils
entities.summary: The Tukaani Project's LZMA2-based compression utilities, packaged in the MSYS environment and split from their shared codec library, liblzma.

entities.name: Zstandard (zstd)
entities.summary: A fast lossless compression algorithm and CLI, packaged in the MSYS environment and split from its shared codec library, libzstd.

entities.name: Info-ZIP Zip
entities.summary: The Info-ZIP archiver that creates PKZIP-compatible .zip archives, packaged in the MSYS environment.

entities.name: Info-ZIP UnZip
entities.summary: The Info-ZIP extractor for PKZIP-compatible .zip archives, packaged in the MSYS environment.

entities.name: p7zip
entities.summary: A command-line port of the 7-Zip archiver (7z format and algorithms originating with Igor Pavlov's 7-Zip), packaged in the MSYS environment.

entities.name: Lzip
entities.summary: A single-file LZMA-based compressor designed around a simple, well-specified format optimized for long-term data safety, packaged in the MSYS environment.

entities.name: GNU Cpio
entities.summary: The GNU implementation of cpio, copying file archives to and from a cpio- or tar-format stream, packaged in the MSYS environment.

entities.name: LZ4
entities.summary: A very fast lossless compression algorithm and CLI prioritizing speed over ratio, packaged in the MSYS environment.

entities.name: GNU Ed
entities.summary: The GNU implementation of ed, the POSIX-mandated line-oriented text editor, packaged in the MSYS environment.

entities.name: GNU Emacs
entities.summary: The extensible, self-documenting display editor, packaged in the MSYS environment as its console (non-GUI-toolkit) build.

entities.name: less
entities.summary: A terminal-based pager for viewing text files a screen at a time, packaged in the MSYS environment.

entities.name: mintty
entities.summary: A terminal emulator with native Windows look and feel, hosting MSYS shell sessions in the MSYS environment.

entities.name: GNU Nano
entities.summary: A small, easy-to-use screen editor descended from Pico, packaged in the MSYS environment.

entities.name: ncurses
entities.summary: The terminal-capability and screen-handling library underlying most of this batch's interactive text-mode programs, packaged in the MSYS environment.

entities.name: Vim
entities.summary: A highly configurable, improved version of the vi text editor, packaged in the MSYS environment.

entities.name: OpenSSH
entities.summary: The free implementation of the SSH protocol suite, packaged in the MSYS environment for secure remote login and file transfer.

properties.role: secure remote login and file transfer

entities.name: curl
entities.summary: A multi-protocol command-line file-transfer client, packaged in the MSYS environment and split from its transfer library, libcurl.

entities.name: Git (MSYS2 package)
entities.summary: The fast distributed version control system, packaged as a plain MSYS2 package — distinct from the separately distributed Git for Windows product documented in Volume 9.
entities.authority: Linus Torvalds / Git community (Junio C Hamano, maintainer)

entities.name: GnuPG
entities.summary: A complete implementation of the OpenPGP standard for encryption and signing, packaged in the MSYS environment.

entities.name: OpenSSL
entities.summary: A general-purpose cryptography and TLS/SSL toolkit, packaged in the MSYS environment and split from its shared cryptographic library, libopenssl.

entities.name: GCC
entities.summary: The GNU Compiler Collection, packaged per native environment (UCRT64 shown here) as the default C/C++/OpenMP compiler driver for MinGW-w64 targets.

entities.name: GNU Binutils
entities.summary: The GNU binary utilities (assembler, linker, and object-file tools), packaged per native environment (UCRT64 shown here) as GCC's default backend toolchain.

entities.name: GDB
entities.summary: The GNU Debugger, packaged per native environment (UCRT64 shown here) as the default debugger for GCC-oriented environments.

entities.name: Clang
entities.summary: The C language family frontend for LLVM, packaged per native environment (CLANG64 shown here) as the default compiler driver for LLVM-oriented MinGW-w64 targets.

entities.name: LLD
entities.summary: The LLVM linker, packaged per native environment (CLANG64 shown here) as Clang's default backend linker.

entities.name: LLDB
entities.summary: The LLVM debugger, packaged per native environment (CLANG64 shown here) as the default debugger for LLVM-oriented environments.

entities.name: CMake
entities.summary: A cross-platform build-system generator, packaged per native environment (UCRT64 shown here), producing native build files (including Ninja) rather than building directly.

entities.name: Meson
entities.summary: A high-productivity build system, packaged per native environment (UCRT64 shown here), generating Ninja build files by default rather than building directly.

entities.name: Ninja
entities.summary: A small, fast build-file executor, packaged per native environment (UCRT64 shown here) and used as the default backend for both CMake and Meson.

entities.name: pkgconf
entities.summary: A pkg-config-compatible library-metadata query tool, packaged per native environment (UCRT64 shown here) as the packaged substitute for the original freedesktop.org pkg-config.

entities.name: GNU Autoconf
entities.summary: An m4-macro-based framework for generating portable configure scripts, packaged in the MSYS environment.

entities.name: GNU Automake
entities.summary: A tool for generating portable Makefile.in files from higher-level Makefile.am descriptions, packaged in the MSYS environment as multiple side-by-side versioned packages dispatched by a wrapper script.

entities.name: GNU Libtool
entities.summary: A generic library-build support script generator, providing a portable interface for building shared and static libraries, packaged in the MSYS environment.

entities.name: GNU Make
entities.summary: A dependency-rule build-file executor, packaged both in the MSYS environment and, separately, as a native build for each MinGW-w64 environment.

entities.name: libstdc++
entities.summary: GCC's C++ standard library implementation, bundled inside the gcc-libs package rather than distributed as a standalone MSYS2 package.

entities.name: libc++
entities.summary: LLVM's C++ standard library implementation, packaged standalone for CLANG64, UCRT64, and MINGW64 rather than bundled with a compiler package.

entities.name: zlib
entities.summary: A general-purpose DEFLATE compression library, packaged per native environment (UCRT64 shown here) and, per this snapshot, the single most-depended-upon library in this knowledge base.

entities.name: GNU libiconv
entities.summary: A character-set conversion library, packaged per native environment (UCRT64 shown here) and depended on across most of this environment's text-processing tools.

entities.name: GNU gettext
entities.summary: The GNU internationalization (NLS) runtime library, packaged per native environment (UCRT64 shown here) as gettext-runtime, separate from the gettext-tools and gettext-libtextstyle packages.

entities.name: Expat
entities.summary: A stream-oriented XML parser library, packaged per native environment (UCRT64 shown here) and used by several other tools documented in this knowledge base (CMake, GDB) for XML-format handling.

entities.name: libxml2
entities.summary: A full-featured XML parsing and toolkit library, packaged per native environment (UCRT64 shown here) with built-in character-set conversion and compressed-XML support.

entities.name: ICU (International Components for Unicode)
entities.summary: A mature Unicode and internationalization library covering text handling, collation, formatting, and locale data, packaged per native environment (UCRT64 shown here).

entities.name: Boost
entities.summary: A large collection of peer-reviewed, portable C++ source libraries, packaged per native environment (UCRT64 shown here) with optional Python-binding support.

entities.name: SQLite
entities.summary: A self-contained, serverless SQL database engine library, packaged per native environment (UCRT64 shown here) and depended on by GnuPG for its key/trust database, among others.

claims.subject: environment:msys2:msys
claims.statement: MSYS is the POSIX-oriented system and package-management environment.

claims.subject: environment:msys2:ucrt64
claims.statement: UCRT64 is the recommended default native MSYS2 environment.

claims.subject: environment:msys2:clang64
claims.statement: CLANG64 uses the UCRT with the LLVM/Clang compiler family and libc++.

claims.subject: environment:msys2:clangarm64
claims.statement: CLANGARM64 uses the UCRT with the LLVM/Clang compiler family and libc++ on AArch64.

claims.subject: environment:msys2:mingw64
claims.statement: MINGW64 is deprecated as of 2026-03-15.

claims.subject: environment:msys2:mingw32
claims.statement: MINGW32 is in phase-out lifecycle status.

claims.subject: component:gnu:bash
claims.statement: The MSYS bash package provides the `sh` command.

claims.subject: component:gnu:coreutils
claims.statement: GNU Coreutils packages the core POSIX-oriented file, shell, and text manipulation utilities for the MSYS environment.

claims.subject: component:gnu:gawk
claims.statement: The MSYS gawk package provides the `awk` command.

claims.subject: component:gnu:findutils
claims.statement: GNU Findutils packages the file-locating and command-construction utilities (including `find` and `xargs`) for the MSYS environment.

claims.subject: component:gnu:gzip
claims.statement: The MSYS gzip package's dependencies on bash and less reflect its bundled shell-script wrappers (zcat, zless, zgrep, zcmp, zdiff) rather than a dependency of the core gzip/gunzip binary itself.

claims.subject: component:bzip2:bzip2
claims.statement: The MSYS bzip2 CLI package is split from and links against libbz2, its shared compression library, rather than bundling the codec statically.

claims.subject: component:info-zip:zip
claims.statement: Zip and UnZip support the bzip2 compression method within .zip archives, explaining their libbz2 dependency.

claims.subject: component:lz4:lz4
claims.statement: The MSYS lz4 package's declared dependency on lz4 itself reflects a version-pinned constraint against its own bundled shared library rather than a distinct dependency package.

claims.subject: component:greenwood:less
claims.statement: less's dependency on libpcre2_8 backs Perl-compatible regular-expression support in its search functionality.

claims.subject: component:vim:vim
claims.statement: Vim's dependency on perl reflects optional built-in Perl-interpreter integration, enabling embedded Perl scripting via :perl.

claims.subject: component:gnu:ncurses
claims.statement: ncurses is the most-depended-upon package observed in this catalog snapshot among the tools modeled in this knowledge base, reflecting its role as the shared terminal-capability library underlying nearly every interactive text-mode program.

claims.subject: component:git:git
claims.statement: Git's runtime dependency on nano reflects its use as a guaranteed-present fallback editor for commit messages and interactive commands when no EDITOR/core.editor/VISUAL is configured, not a build-time requirement of Git's own functionality.

claims.subject: component:git:git
claims.statement: The git component modeled in this volume is the plain MSYS2-packaged git, distinct from the separately distributed Git for Windows product documented in Volume 9; both distributions track upstream Git 2.55.0 as of their respective 2026-07-29 and 2026-07-30 observations, but have separate package and release provenance.

claims.subject: component:gnu:gcc
claims.statement: GCC's dependencies on gmp, mpfr, and mpc back arbitrary-precision arithmetic used during compilation (for example, constant folding), and its dependency on isl backs the Graphite loop-optimization framework.

claims.subject: component:gnu:binutils
claims.statement: Binutils' dependencies on zlib and zstd back compressed debug-section support (--compress-debug-sections=zlib|zstd).

claims.subject: component:gnu:gdb
claims.statement: GDB's dependency on python backs its Python scripting API (pretty-printers, gdb.execute), and its optional dependency on python-pygments backs syntax-highlighted source-code display.

claims.subject: component:llvm:lldb
claims.statement: LLDB's dependency on python backs its Python scripting API, the same scripting-extensibility pattern documented for GDB.

claims.subject: component:llvm:lld
claims.statement: The MSYS2 lld package declares that it provides the binutils virtual capability in the CLANG64 environment, letting packages that depend on a generic binutils-like toolchain resolve against LLD instead of GNU Binutils.

claims.subject: component:cmake:cmake
claims.statement: CMake's dependencies map to specific built-in features: cppdap backs its --debugger Debug Adapter Protocol support, curl backs file(DOWNLOAD)/ExternalProject network operations, jsoncpp backs its JSON-based file-api and CMakePresets.json support, libarchive backs file(ARCHIVE_CREATE) and CPack archive generation, and rhash backs its file(<HASH>) commands.

claims.subject: component:mesonbuild:meson
claims.statement: Meson's dependency on ninja reflects Ninja as its default and primary build backend: Meson generates build files that Ninja executes rather than compiling directly.

claims.subject: component:pkgconf:pkgconf
claims.statement: The MSYS2 pkgconf package provides, conflicts with, and replaces pkg-config in this environment, making pkgconf the packaged substitute for the original freedesktop.org pkg-config tool.

claims.subject: component:gnu:autoconf
claims.statement: Autoconf is fundamentally an m4 macro-processing framework: autoconf/autoheader/autoreconf expand m4 macros to generate a portable configure script, which explains its dependency on m4.

claims.subject: component:gnu:automake
claims.statement: MSYS2 packages automake as multiple side-by-side versioned packages (automake1.11 through automake1.18 in this snapshot), with automake-wrapper acting as a version-dispatching frontend that provides the generic automake/aclocal commands.

claims.subject: component:gnu:libtool
claims.statement: Libtool's primary artifact, the project-local libtool script, is itself a generated shell script executed via bash, which explains the package's dependency on bash.

claims.subject: library:gnu:libstdc++
claims.statement: libstdc++ is not packaged as a standalone MSYS2 package; it is bundled inside gcc-libs alongside libgcc, libgomp, and other GCC runtime support libraries.

claims.subject: library:llvm:libc++
claims.statement: In CLANG64, the libc++ package itself provides the gcc-libs/cc-libs virtual capability, since no separate GCC runtime package exists in that environment; in UCRT64, libc++ instead depends on the cc-libs capability that gcc-libs provides there.

claims.subject: library:llvm:libc++
claims.statement: libc++ is packaged for UCRT64 and MINGW64 as well as CLANG64, meaning a project can opt into libc++ even in a GCC-oriented environment rather than being restricted to libstdc++.

claims.subject: library:gnu:zlib
claims.statement: zlib is the most-depended-upon package observed in this catalog snapshot among all components and libraries modeled in this knowledge base, with 299 recorded reverse dependents, exceeding gcc-libs' 167.

claims.subject: library:gnu:gettext
claims.statement: GNU gettext is split into three separate MSYS2 packages: gettext-runtime (the libintl runtime library), gettext-tools (msgfmt/xgettext/msginit and other CLI tools), and gettext-libtextstyle (a terminal text-styling library used by the tools); this page models the runtime component.

claims.subject: library:gnome:libxml2
claims.statement: libxml2's dependencies on libiconv and zlib back its character-encoding conversion and compressed-XML (gzip) reading support respectively.

claims.subject: library:sqlite:sqlite3
claims.statement: SQLite's dependency on tcl reflects its own canonical test-suite tooling, which is Tcl-based, bundled into this package rather than a runtime requirement of the SQL engine itself.
